Control weakness: No duplicate-payment detection in the payment run
Detection rule: Same VendorID + identical debit amount (to the cent) + identical invoice reference in the journal description + posting dates within 30 days; reversal pairs excluded.
Follow-up: Obtain the supplier statement and both remittances; request a credit note or refund for the second payment.

Assertion tested: Validity of the vendor; occurrence of the payment
Control weakness: Vendor master created and bank details changed without independent approval
Detection rule: Vendor master flagged employee-linked (name or bank detail matches the employee master), created within 180 days of first payment, no tax clearance and 7-day terms. Exception = a payment to such a vendor that bypassed the accounts-payable payment run and carries no approver.
Follow-up: Freeze the vendor pending verification of ownership; obtain contracts, deliverables and bank mandate; confirm the employee relationship.

Control weakness: Approval limits enforced on the transaction, not the commitment
Detection rule: Debit of $4,985-$4,995 or $9,750-$9,999 posted to a procurement expense account (payroll excluded) against a named vendor, where the amount is a round number (no cents, multiple of $5).
Follow-up: Confirm whether a PO or approval exists; test whether the same vendor received other payments in the same week that together exceed the limit.

Scheme: One purchase split into two invoices
Control weakness: Purchase-order threshold tested per invoice, not per order
Detection rule: Two or more payments to the same vendor, same expense account, identical amount to the cent, posted within 5 days, each between $3,000 and $7,000, where the pair exceeds the $5,000 purchase-order threshold.
Follow-up: Obtain the goods-received notes and the quotations; confirm whether one order was split; report to procurement management.

Scheme: Manual journals posted outside business hours
Control weakness: No monitoring of posting times; suspense account used as a clearing account
Detection rule: Manual journal entered on a Saturday or Sunday, or before 07:00 or after 22:00, with no approver recorded, that debits a P&L account and credits the suspense account (1990).
Follow-up: Obtain the supporting document and the reason for the timing; confirm who authorised it; reverse if unsupported.

Scheme: AP clerk posting revenue credit notes
TestName: Segregation of duties - user / account matrix
Control weakness: User access rights wider than the job role requires
Detection rule: Journal prepared by a user whose role is 'Accounts Payable Clerk' containing a line posted to a Revenue account.
Follow-up: Review the user's system rights; obtain the credit-note documentation; re-perform the affected revenue entries.

Control weakness: No periodic review of the prepayment schedule
Detection rule: Manual journal that debits a prepayment account (1300) and credits an expense account, with no opposite entry of the same amount in the following 60 days.
Follow-up: Agree the prepayment schedule to the underlying contracts; reverse the entries that have no supporting asset.
